summary: Nira Wickramasinghe is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at the University of Paris (~1981–1985) and the University of Oxford (~1985–1989). Around 2010, she was appointed Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University.

Nirajan Kafle specializes in Indology. He studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyaupane, completing his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter Bisschop in 2015. He held posts at the University of Naples (2019) and Leiden (2021).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti studied at Cambridge (Ph.D. ~1924–1926), Paris, and Berlin. An Indology and history/archaeology scholar, he held posts at Calcutta, Paris, Berlin, and the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Director General from 1948 to 1950.

Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

Nirbhay N. Singh works in religious and Buddhist studies. He has served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).

Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency College (~1930–1934). He taught at Krishnath College and Calcutta (1971), and served as founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987).
Nirupam Chakma is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), where he studied under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.
Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under the doctoral supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and completed a D.Phil. at Wolfson College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich in 2003. She later served as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima was an Indologist and historian who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo (B.A. ~1958, Litt.D. 1993). He taught at Tokyo (Professor Emeritus 1981–1994) and Taisho University (~1994–2008), and presided over the Epigraphical Society of India (1985).

Noboru Miyata was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history who studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba. He held professorships at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1970–1979), Tsukuba (~1979–1999), and Kanagawa University (~1999–2000).
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and later served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe, Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, and Ichijo Ogawa, later serving as professor at Otani University and its Junior College.

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 1962) under Yutaka Ochihara. He held assistant professorial posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1988–2001). After serving as a Research Fellow at Tokyo, he became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed research student training at Taisho University and held an appointment as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from ~1955 to 1959 and later held a post there as an assistant professor (attested 1972).

Tensho Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2009) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2009–2012) and the University of Tokyo (~2012–2016).

Nobumi Iyanaga is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969). He taught at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and held a research contract at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2008–2014).
Nobuo Otsuka is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University between ~1983 and 1988, and later served as a researcher there (attested 1995).
